artboards.role: The single artboard delivered by this ingest. The linked node is a FRAME (not a CANVAS), so there are no sibling artboards to separate out — header, cart body (order list + delivery form + order summary) and footer are all sections of this one 'cart' screen, not independent screens.

open_questions.topic: No empty-cart / zero-quantity state is designed
open_questions.detail: The frame only shows a populated cart (3 line items, quantities 2/1/1) with active '-' / '+' / Remove controls. Nothing defines what the order card, item count, subtotal or checkout button should show once every item has been removed.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume decrementing a QuantityStepper below 1 (or pressing Remove) deletes that CartLineItem row, and if all rows are removed the order card falls back to a simple 'Your cart is empty' message in place of the item list, with 'Proceed to Checkout' disabled.

options.label: Plain 'Your cart is empty' text replacing the item list — lowest-effort, matches no other empty state in this frame
Redirect/prompt back to Our Menu when the cart empties — avoids ever rendering an empty cart card
Disable '-' at quantity 1 so the cart can only be emptied via Remove, deferring the empty-state question to the Remove flow only

open_questions.topic: QuantityStepper has no drawn disabled/min-boundary state
open_questions.detail: All three stepper instances (13:275, 13:292, 13:309) render their '-' button identically regardless of value, including the two currently at quantity 1. It is unclear whether '-' should disable at 1 (forcing Remove for deletion) or continue below 1 to remove the row.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume '-' remains enabled at quantity 1 and decrementing past 1 removes the line item (equivalent to pressing Remove), since no visually distinct disabled button style exists anywhere in the frame's token set to represent the alternative.

options.label: '-' at quantity 1 removes the row — no new disabled-button style needed, matches assumption
'-' disables (dimmed) at quantity 1, forcing explicit 'Remove' for deletion — requires a new disabled-button visual not present in the frame

open_questions.topic: Header cart badge value's basis is ambiguous
open_questions.detail: The header CartIconButton badge (13:262) reads '3', matching the order card's '3 Items' line-item count (13:268) but NOT the sum of unit quantities across the three lines (2 + 1 + 1 = 4). A reader could reasonably wire the badge to either number.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume the badge always mirrors the count of distinct line items in the cart (matching '3 Items'), not the summed quantity of units.

options.label: Distinct line-item count (3) — matches the '3 Items' text and the badge's current value exactly
Summed unit quantity (4) — more common e-commerce convention but does not match the badge's drawn value of 3

open_questions.topic: Only the 'Applied' success state of PromoCodeField is drawn
open_questions.detail: The Promo Code field (13:362–370) is shown pre-filled with 'FORNOROSSO10' and a green 'Applied' state. No default empty/unfilled state, no in-progress state, and no invalid-code error state are present anywhere in the frame.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assume a default state (empty input, neutral #F3EFE9 border, an inactive 'Apply' button in place of 'Applied') and an error state (vivid-red #C82D25 border + inline error text, reusing the field-error pattern implied by the frame's vivid/stroke tokens) for invalid codes.

options.label: Derive default/error states from tokens already in this frame (#F3EFE9 neutral border for default, #C82D25 for error) — no new colors introduced
Block PromoCodeField implementation on new Figma states for default/error before building anything beyond the applied view

open_questions.topic: SiteHeader / SiteFooter may be out of scope for a cart-item-management story
open_questions.detail: The ingested frame is a full page including global header and footer chrome, but the story (MT-STORY-028: cart item management) is likely scoped to the cart-body interactions (line items, quantity, remove, promo, summary). Building SiteHeader/SiteFooter here risks duplicating work already planned under a separate layout/navigation story.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Map and list SiteHeader/SiteFooter in this component map for completeness (per instruction to map every APP-CONTENT node), but assume the implementer will confirm with the team whether these are already owned by another story before building new components for them.

open_questions.topic: Footer social icons have no destination URLs in the Figma data
open_questions.detail: instagram/facebook/twitter icon buttons (13:385, 13:388, 13:391) are purely visual Vector nodes with no link annotations in the ingested frame.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Render SocialIconRow icons as inert placeholders (no href) until real social URLs are supplied.

open_questions.topic: Delivery form fields show filled-in sample data, not placeholders
open_questions.detail: Street Address ('128 Pizzaiolo Boulevard'), Apt/Suite ('Penthouse 4B') and Special Delivery Instructions all render as populated text in the frame. It's unclear whether this is real returning-user data, a placeholder/example, or fixture content for the mockup.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Treat the three values as example placeholder text for the prototype, not implying a 'returning user with saved address' feature.
